text.p: These are the leading stories in the Egyptian press on Thursday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.

- Government to prospose 11 draft laws to encourage investment, simplify its procedures and protect the national economy. Prime Minister Kamal Ganzouri heads a cabinet meeting, says the government has also finished drafting laws affecting free zones and companies. State to remove 82 percent of buildings illegally constructed on agricultural lands.
- President Mubarak and President Clinton will discuss revitalising the peace process when they meet in Washington on March 10.
- Mubarak, Palestinian President Arafat and Israeli Prime Minister Netanyahu to hold first tripartite meeting since the Hebron agreement at World Economic Forum in Davos.
- Government to increase by 66 percent the budget for infrastructure projects in new communities.
- World Economic Forum says Gamal Mubarak is a future leader.

- Cabinet meeting drafts working paper on the future of Egypt. State to plant 250,000 acres (115,000 hectares) in the new delta and 260,000 acres in Oweinat oasis within the year. Eleven new laws to simplify investment procedures and create an economic boom. Egypt to set up a fund for the protection of expatriate Egyptians.
- Mubarak and Gambian leader hold final session of talks in Cairo airport.
- Mubarak's participation in the World Economic Forum will open new horizons for the Egyptian economy.
- Egypt's minister of supply sets new season's price for Giza 45 cotton at 1,000 pounds ($295) per qantar. He says Japan has asked to buy all available quantities of this variety. (1 qantar = 50 kg)

- Cabinet meeting headed by Ganzouri decides that all decisions and draft laws made in 1996 will be implemented immediately. State to pay unable farmers half the cost of infrastructure needed at their farms.
- Mubarak tells transportation minister to start work on plans for an underground train in Alexandria.
- Mubarak to give an important speech at Davos.
